C-ROOT-WINDOW.Summary:
One engine file, `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts`, plus its suite `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`. The bundle pays four live findings — `F216`, `F182`, `F193`, `F190`, read by id from the parsed `findings.xml`, not from the brief — whose owners name a later charter and whose remedy is, together, the record engine's root-window arithmetic, and it pre-pays two staged findings (`F225`, `F226`) that are not in the record: the findings genre has five lines of headroom at this commit (measured; expired the moment the predecessor's flush merged), so neither staged entry can flush here, and this bundle's own registry row names both in `<Pays>` anyway. The deliverables, each measured against the shipped engine at this commit:
**The root-rewrite mode (`F216`).** The shipped engine rewrites an existing record's roots only inside the `--retire` move, which returns early when nothing is eligible (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1150`), so every ordinary record write obliges a hand-written root — `F216`'s recorded condition, verified live at this commit. The bundle charters a `--rewrite-roots` mode that re-derives, for each of the four live genre roots, `base` from its shipped metric read back (`newlineCount` for findings and rulings, the live-`Entry` rule for the index, the live `Row` count for the registry) and `headroom` as ceiling minus base, while **holding** the persisted ceiling — the ceiling attribute passes through byte-for-byte, so the mode can neither raise a ceiling (`D28`) nor adopt or recompute one. The mode refuses (exit non-zero, nothing written) when any live genre's count exceeds its persisted ceiling — the one state whose only remedy is the move, which is the only shipped writer that opens a window — and when a ceiling attribute is missing or unreadable (`AC-MODE-SHIPPED`). Driven on throwaway copies at this commit: a byte no-op on a consistent record, refusal with an untouched file in both refuse cases, and a held hand-raised ceiling left byte-identical rather than adopted — the laundering boundary stated, not hidden (`Known boundary` below). The plan's own row-mint task rewrites the registry roots with this mode, so the last hand-written root this lineage records is a predecessor's, not this bundle's.
**The floored derivation (`F182`).** `7 × median` persists a fractional ceiling whenever the live population is even and its two middles differ by an odd number — the shipped `median()` returns that half (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:124`) and the multiplier decides whether it survives. The shipped engine carries the defect at all four derivation sites: `:596` and `:597` (the `--split` path) and `:1224` and `:1225` (the `--retire` path). This bundle floors the derivation at all four sites. Rounding **down** is argued in `F182` as the only direction that cannot loosen a budget, and that argument is verified against the shipped clamp (`persistSnapshot`, `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:950`): the clamp takes `min(persisted ceiling, base + headroom)`, and headroom is ceiling minus base, so a larger formula term can only hold or raise the persisted ceiling — equal-or-looser — and only rounding down cannot loosen. Driven both directions on a synthetic record whose post-move population is even with middles 19 and 20: the shipped engine persists `ceiling="269.5"` / `headroom="145.5"`, the chartered engine persists `269` / `145`. Declared as a typed `Clarification` (`INV-ROOT-WINDOW-ROUNDING`), not decided silently.
**The unmoved-genre window rule (`F193`).** On any successful move the shipped engine rewrites all four live roots, and for a genre where nothing moved the clamp persists `min(previous ceiling, base + H)` — the window a retirement opened is clamped back to `H` by the next move in any other genre. Measured live today: the shipped engine, driven on a synthetic record where the rulings genre's window (54 lines) exceeds its `H` (28), clamps the rulings ceiling from 60 to 34 in response to a findings-only move — `F193`'s table, reproduced. The remedy this bundle charters is **persisting the opened window**: a genre the move did not change keeps its persisted ceiling while its base is re-derived from the shipped metric read back, so the window survives every unrelated move and the whole record still leaves the move satisfying the shipped all-roots tripwire (`base + headroom = ceiling`, `base` equals its metric) — the invariant the shipped `T-001 window` test asserts at `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:692` and the production roots invariant assert, which the runner-up candidate (re-deriving only the genre that moved) would weaken, because the shipped validator has no base-versus-metric check and a drifted unmoved genre would survive a legitimate move with the validator green. Driven across two consecutive unrelated retirements on a throwaway copy: the rulings genre stays byte-identical through both. Declared as a typed `Clarification` (`INV-ROOT-WINDOW-UNMOVED`), with this recommendation in its text; it governs `AC-WINDOW-UNMOVED` and `AC-RECORD-UNMOVED`, and the plan cannot be approved over it.
**The normalising pass (`F190`).** `--retire`'s span removal deletes an element's span without consuming the removed element's leading indent, so every survivor after a removed sibling gains two spaces and the drift compounds (`F190`, measured live: the production `rulings.xml` carries five elements at 4-space indent today — `d5.2`, `d6`, `d9.1`, `d19`, `d25`). The bundle adds a normalising pass to the move's writer: for each file the move wrote (a genre with removals, a retired sibling with appends), the inter-element whitespace is rewritten to the canonical house shape — `<newline><two spaces>` before each top-level element, `<newline>` before the root close tag — and every surviving element's own bytes pass through untouched. Driven at this commit: after the close's move, all 210 surviving `<Finding>` elements are byte-identical to their pre-close bytes by parse, only the gaps changed, the appended retired-side elements sit at 2-space indent with the root close at column 0, and the shipped preservation validator exits 0 (`AC-INDENT-NORMALISED`).
**The payment and the close.** The plan mints this bundle's registry row — `kind="chartered"`, `<Pays>F216 F182 F193 F190 F225 F226</Pays>`, a `<StatusText>` carrying no `F` token and no `Closed with` sentence (`F197`'s law: the shipped `closedWithTokens` at `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:338` mints payments from an archived row's `StatusText` prose, and ordering cannot escape it) — and rewrites the registry roots with the new mode. At the close, the ceremony's move runs for real, and its byte-move table is measured, not assumed: exactly five of the seven record files change bytes — `findings.xml` (four elements removed, roots rewritten, gaps normalised), `findings-retired.xml` (four appended, normalised), `registry.xml` (the row removed, roots rewritten, normalised), `registry-retired.xml` (the row appended, normalised), `decisions.xml` (four `<Entry>` layers flip, roots rewritten) — while `rulings.xml` and `rulings-retired.xml` stay byte-identical (no ruling moves; under the chartered engine the unmoved rulings root is re-spliced from the held ceiling and the read-back base, which equals its persisted bytes at any tripwire-consistent record), and the stub `decisions.md` and `record-inventory.json` are untouched by any shipped writer in the window. The pre-payment of `F225` and `F226` is sound and verified from the shipped code before this spec relies on it: `derivePayerMap` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:403`) keys its map by token with no requirement that a matching `<Finding>` element exist, and eligibility requires only that the payer name an archive directory (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1102`) — measured: the shipped payer map at this commit mints none of the six tokens, so this bundle's row mints all six; after the close the map mints `F225` and `F226` to `C-ROOT-WINDOW` while zero elements with those tokens exist in either findings file, and a second `--retire` reports `moved 0`. The close frees the findings genre: the driven post-close window is 135 lines against the two staged entries' 37 and 69 rendered element lines, so the next flush can land both.
C-ROOT-WINDOW.Problem:
The four findings this bundle pays state, between them, the whole root arithmetic of the record engine, and each names this bundle as owner in its own `Owner:` line. They are the payment queue's head (`F216` first), and the suite's liveness pins were repaired to payment-invariance in PR #86 precisely so that this payment could happen without reddening the shipped suite (`F225`, measured: the shipped flush invariant no longer pins any named finding `live`).
**`F216` — roots are hand-maintained on every write.** The only code that rewrites an existing record's roots sits inside the `--retire` move after its `movedCount === 0` early return (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1150`); `--split` writes roots only onto a newly created record. Every record-touching bundle since the split has hand-written its roots — the history the finding records. The remedy is a mode that rewrites roots from the shipped relations without requiring a move, so the tripwire's correctness stops depending on nobody miscounting.
**`F182` — the fractional ceiling.** The findings genre has shipped `7 × median` since the split and its median is currently the integer 34 over 214 live elements (middles 34 and 34 — measured at this commit), which is the only reason no fractional ceiling has persisted yet; the rulings genre's retire-path formula became `7 × median` the same way (`:1225`), and its 27 H2-level live decisions give the odd-count median 37. One parity flip in either population persists a half line into a public methodology record. The remedy is a rounding rule at the point of derivation; the direction is a design question the finding itself flags, resolved here as a typed `Clarification` with the rounding-down argument verified against the shipped clamp rather than adopted from the finding's prose.
**`F193` — the evaporating window.** The shipped engine rewrites all four live roots on any successful move, and the clamp (`persistSnapshot`, `:950`) takes the smaller of the persisted ceiling and `pre-move base + H` — for a genre where nothing moved that is exactly `min(previous window, H)`. The findings genre's post-close window (135 lines, driven) is what makes the next flush of `F225` and `F226` possible; under the shipped engine, one unrelated retirement anywhere would take it back down to `H`. The remedy candidates are the finding's own two; this spec declares the hole typed (`INV-ROOT-WINDOW-UNMOVED`) with the measured recommendation above, and the close-bound criteria are written to hold under the recommendation while naming the file set the runner-up would leave untouched.
**`F190` — the compounding indent.** The live record already carries the drift: five `rulings.xml` elements at 4-space indent, measured at this commit. The remedy is a normalising pass in the writer — not the hand edit that restored `registry.xml`'s close tag during the `C-PAYMENT-RECORD` close, and not the canonical serializer `F221` charters (a separate, larger deliverable with its own owner).
**The timing constraint that makes this bundle the payment vehicle.** The findings genre has five lines of headroom at this commit — the tightest a flush of the predecessor's flush set could leave — so `F225` (37 rendered element lines) and `F226` (69) cannot flush until a payment frees room, and the first payment the queue opens with is this bundle's own `<Pays>` set. The pre-payment is what makes the next flush possible at all; that is why the row names both staged tokens.

Goals.Goal: The mode. `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` gains a `--rewrite-roots` mode, `rewriteRecordRoots`, wired beside `--retire` in `main()`. For each of the four live genre roots it derives `base` from the shipped metric read back, holds the persisted ceiling — the ceiling attribute passes through byte-for-byte, never recomputed — and persists `headroom = ceiling − base` through the same `withRootSnapshot` splice the move uses. It refuses, before any write, when any live genre's count exceeds its persisted ceiling (message names the genre, both counts, and the move as the remedy) and when a ceiling attribute is missing or unreadable; it re-derives all four live roots or none. Retired siblings carry no root attributes and are not touched; the stub and the inventory are not touched. Driven at this commit on throwaway copies, both directions: a byte no-op on the consistent production record; exit 1 with the file untouched when the findings ceiling is set below its base; exit 1 when the registry ceiling attribute is removed; a hand-raised registry ceiling held byte-identical (`Known boundary` below states what that does not repair). The plan's row-mint task runs this mode on the production record to write the registry roots after minting the row — the registry root's `base` moves from 12 to the read-back and `headroom` becomes the remainder, with the other three live roots byte-identical — driven on a copy first, then verified by the shipped relations on the record.

The floored derivation. All four headroom derivation sites floor their product: `Math.floor(7 × median(...))` at the two findings sites and `Math.floor(…)` at the two rulings sites (`--split` at `:596`–`:597`, `--retire` at `:1224`–`:1225` in the shipped file). The registry (15) and index (40) headrooms are already integers and are not touched. Driven on the synthetic even-population record: shipped `ceiling="269.5"`, chartered `269` — the same drive discriminates, not a unit-only assertion.

The unmoved-genre window rule, under `INV-ROOT-WINDOW-UNMOVED`'s recommendation: on a successful move, a genre with zero moved elements keeps its persisted ceiling and gets its base re-derived from its shipped metric read back (`headroom` becomes the remainder); a genre with moved elements keeps the shipped `persistSnapshot` arithmetic with the pre-move base as the ceiling term and the floored headroom. The index is re-derived whenever its `<Entry>` layers flip, and the retired siblings — which carry no root attributes — are written only when the move appended to them. Driven: the findings-only close leaves the four live roots tripwire-consistent with `rulings.xml` and `rulings-retired.xml` byte-identical; two consecutive unrelated retirements leave `rulings.xml` byte-identical through both.

The normalising pass in the move's writer: `normaliseGaps` rewrites only the inter-element whitespace of a file the move wrote, to the canonical house shape the split renderer produces (`<newline><two spaces>` before each top-level element, `<newline>` before the root close, the tail after the root close preserved). Element bytes are passed through from the parser-derived spans, so the pass changes no element's bytes — driven: every surviving `<Finding>` element byte-identical across the close by parse, the appended retired-side elements at 2-space indent, both root close tags at column 0, the shipped preservation validator green on the moved record. The pass is scoped to the files the move wrote; a genre with zero moved elements keeps its bytes untouched, so the five 4-space-indented `rulings.xml` elements stay until a rulings move normalises them — measured, and stated rather than hidden.

The row and the payment. The plan mints the row into the live registry exactly as the house shape has it (`<Row name="C-ROOT-WINDOW" status="live" kind="chartered">` with `<Number />`, `<Charter>` carrying the searched-before-minting statement, `<Pays>F216 F182 F193 F190 F225 F226</Pays>`, `<StatusText>` carrying no `F` token and no `Closed with` sentence) and rewrites the registry roots with the chartered mode. At the close the ceremony's move reports five moves: the four named findings, each stamped `<PaidBy>C-ROOT-WINDOW</PaidBy>` in the retired sibling, and the row itself; four index `<Entry>` layers flip; and the six-token payer map mints `F225` and `F226` to this bundle with zero matching elements in the record — the pre-payment waiting for the next flush, measured sound from the shipped derivation and eligibility code.

The suite. The plan rewrites the shipped assertions the engine change reddens — measured on a throwaway copy at this commit: `T-001 min not decorative: hand-shrunk findings persist ceiling = Base_live + H without a findings move` (it pins `F193`'s shipped clamp — the very behaviour this bundle fixes — and is rewritten to assert window survival under `INV-ROOT-WINDOW-UNMOVED`'s resolution), the `C-RECORD-PARSE golden` byte fixture (re-captured against the chartered engine's bytes — the bounded one-time reflow `F221` prices), and the `C-RECORD-PARSE payer derivation` baseline map (extended with the row's minted tokens exactly as the shipped test extends it for `F205`/`C-INDEX-METRIC-2`). Known boundary, stated rather than hidden. The mode holds ceilings and cannot repair a hand-raised one: a ceiling above the formula's term is shape-identical to a window a legitimate move opened, so no derivation can distinguish them, and the mode leaves it byte-identical rather than adopting or recomputing it (driven). The raised-and-repaired ceiling therefore survives the mode; it is lowered only by its own genre's next move, whose clamp takes the smaller term. Detection beyond the shipped `RULINGS_PROVENANCE_CEILING` check (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:446`, which covers the rulings genre only) is a distinct deliverable with no design paid for — re-assigned in `NonGoals` under `D11`'s rule, with the mode's structural never-raise and never-adopt as the partial answer this bundle ships. A hand-written base or headroom anywhere is repaired by the next move or the mode; a hand-raised ceiling is not. Read-backs above a held ceiling stop the task and report; they never raise a ceiling and never trim a body.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Flushing `F225` or `F226`, writing or pruning `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md`, or rendering any staged entry into the record. Owner: the next flush bundle's charter; post-merge hygiene, the authority's. The findings genre's post-close window (driven: 135 lines) fits both staged entries' rendered element sizes (37 and 69, measured by the shipped parser rule over the buffer), which is the pre-payment's point — but landing them is the next flush's act under the `D30` window, never this bundle's.

The canonical serializer `F221` charters, and any byte-invariance regime beyond what the close's byte-move table measured: the normalising pass here is scoped to the move's writer, not the serializer, and the record's remaining whitespace drift (the five 4-space-indented `rulings.xml` elements) stays until a rulings move. Owner: `F221`'s chartered bundle.

A provenance or detection mechanism for hand-raised ceilings beyond the shipped `RULINGS_PROVENANCE_CEILING`: the mode holds ceilings and does not adopt them, the move lowers a hand-raised ceiling only in its own genre, and closing the raised-and-repaired detection gap for the other three genres needs a design this spec does not charter. Owner: a later charter, sequenced by the maintainer; the dependency is the mode's shipped hold semantics, and the conflict is `D28`'s never-raise, which forbids the cheapest "remedy".

Changing the split path's rulings headroom multiplier, minting any other row, paying any other token, or touching the eligibility scans, `INDEX_HEADROOM_ENTRIES`, the registry's live-row budget, the provenance constant, or the `--split` mode's behaviour beyond the floor. The split-path rulings formula (`2 × median`, `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:597`) disagrees with the retire-path formula (`7 × median`, `:1225`) — measured at this commit and staged for the authority with its evidence, not in this spec's scope: a root-rewrite surface must use the retire path's `7 ×` because the retire path is the shipped writer of existing-record ceilings and the provenance constant anchors the rulings ceiling to that path's correction, while the split path writes a newly created record only. The bundle that reunifies them owns the call; this one does not.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-MODE-SHIPPED:
The `--rewrite-roots` mode exists in `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` beside `--retire` in `main()` and behaves as chartered: on a record whose live roots satisfy the shipped relations it is a byte no-op (all four live roots re-spliced from the held ceilings and the metric read-backs, which equal the persisted values); it refuses with exit 1 and no write when any live genre's count exceeds its persisted ceiling, and when a live root's ceiling attribute is missing or unreadable; it writes `headroom = ceiling − base` with `base` equal to the shipped metric read back (`newlineCount` for findings and rulings, the live-`Entry` rule for the index, the live `Row` count for the registry) and never writes a ceiling attribute different from the one it read. Content question, answered by driving the real CLI on throwaway copies in both directions (all four driven at this commit; the refusal message names the genre, both counts, and the move as the remedy). Failure: the mode writing a ceiling above the persisted one, a raise by recomputation, a silent clamp-and-continue on an exceeded genre, or a refusal that fires on a consistent record. The instrument is the production assertion the later plan adds, driving the mode against isolated records for the refuse cases and the byte no-op, in the suite's house shape. This criterion is invariant under the close: the close's ceremony does not run the mode, and the mode's presence and refusals are observable in the applied-archive state by the suite.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-ROUNDING-FLOOR:
Every headroom derivation site in `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` floors its product with `Math.floor` — the two findings sites and the two rulings sites, both the `--split` path and the `--retire` path — so no persisted `headroom` or `ceiling` is fractional. Clarifications.Clarification: Resolved 2026-09-11 by the maintainer, as recommended: a genre the move did not change keeps its persisted ceiling; `base` is re-derived from its shipped metric read back and `headroom` is the remainder. The moving genre keeps the shipped `persistSnapshot` arithmetic. One rule, shared by the move and the mode. `F193`'s window semantics for a genre with zero moved elements. Two candidates were driven on throwaway copies at this commit. **Recommendation — persist the opened window (hold the ceiling, re-derive the base):** a genre the move did not change keeps its persisted ceiling and gets `base` from its shipped metric read back, `headroom` as the remainder; the moving genre keeps the shipped `persistSnapshot` arithmetic. Pros: the shipped all-roots tripwire (`base + headroom = ceiling`, `base` equals its metric — asserted after every successful move by the shipped `T-001 window` test at `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:692` and by the production roots invariant) stays true without depending on anyone running the mode, so the move remains self-healing for hand-drift in every genre; the fix is one rule shared with the mode; only the one shipped test that pins the clamp (the `min not decorative` test) needs rewriting, and the moving-genre window test passes unchanged. Cons: the unmoved genre's open-tag splice makes its byte-identity empirical rather than structural (measured byte-identical at any consistent record; a drifted record reddens the criterion and stops the close — the honest outcome), and a hand-raised ceiling in an unmoved genre now survives unrelated moves (it is lowered by its own genre's next move — stated in the Known-boundary `Constraint`). **Runner-up — re-derive only the genre that moved:** pros: the unmoved genre is structurally untouched, so its byte-invariance is structural; cons: it abandons the shipped invariant that every live root satisfies the relations after any successful move — the shipped validator has no base-versus-metric check, so a drifted unmoved genre would survive a legitimate move with the validator green, and the drift would surface only later in the production tripwire; three shipped tests need rewriting instead of one. The runner-up loses because its only advantage (structural byte-invariance for one file) is bought by weakening a shipped invariant the record's enforcement posture relies on, and the same cleanliness is reachable under the recommendation by parse-based relations. Governs `AC-WINDOW-UNMOVED` and, for the byte-invariance reasoning, `AC-RECORD-UNMOVED`.

Resolved 2026-09-11 by the maintainer, as recommended: round down (`Math.floor`) at every derivation site. On an integer median the floor is the identity; on a `.5` median it is the only direction that cannot loosen a budget. `F182`'s rounding direction. **Recommendation — round down (`Math.floor`) at every derivation site:** verified against the shipped clamp (`persistSnapshot`, `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:950`): the persisted ceiling is `min(persisted ceiling, base + headroom)` and headroom is ceiling minus base, so a larger formula term can only hold or raise the persisted ceiling — equal-or-looser — and only rounding down can never loosen a budget; on an integer median the floor is the identity, so the fix changes nothing today. Pros: budgets tighten or hold, never loosen; the relation survives every later move. Cons: the persisted window can be one line tighter than the unfloored arithmetic would have given on a `.5` median — that is the point. **Runner-up — round half up (`Math.round`):** on a `.5` it rounds away from the tighter budget, which is exactly the direction `D28` forbids loosening in; **half-to-even** rounds down or up by parity, so it can loosen and is refused by the same argument. The runner-ups lose on direction, not on style. Governs `AC-ROUNDING-FLOOR`.

Resolved 2026-09-11 by the maintainer, as recommended: `--rewrite-roots` holds every ceiling byte-for-byte, re-derives `base` from the shipped metric and `headroom` as the remainder, and refuses (exit 1, nothing written) when a genre's count exceeds its persisted ceiling or a ceiling attribute is missing. Together with the resolution above this ratifies the record's invariant: a ceiling is written only by `--retire`, and only downward; every other writer holds it. The mode's ceiling semantics. **Recommendation — hold (pass through):** `--rewrite-roots` never writes a ceiling attribute different from the one it read; it re-derives `base` from the shipped metric and `headroom` as ceiling minus base, and refuses (exit 1, nothing written) when a genre's count exceeds its persisted ceiling or a ceiling attribute is missing. Pros: structurally incapable of raising a ceiling (`D28`), incapable of adopting or recomputing one, and it repairs exactly the hand-drift `F216` records — the post-write registry state (base grown, ceiling held, headroom the remainder) is what every hand-write has produced since the split, driven. Cons: it cannot lower a hand-raised ceiling — the Known-boundary `Constraint` states what that leaves open. **Runner-up — formula with clamp (re-derive the ceiling as `min(persisted, base + floored H)`):** pros: lowers hand-raises back to the formula. Cons: it closes every window a retirement opened whenever the formula's term has fallen below the persisted ceiling — `F193`'s defect reintroduced through the mode, the exact behaviour this bundle exists to stop — and on a normal post-write record, where the formula's term exceeds the held ceiling, the clamp reduces to the hold anyway. The runner-up loses on the record's own design. Governs `AC-MODE-SHIPPED`.
